examples.text: „Der indikativische präteritale Flexionsstamm wird bei regelmäßigen Verben sowie bei den unregelmäßigen Verben backen, mahlen, salzen, sollen, spalten und wollen durch Hinzufügen des Präteritalsuffixes te zum indikativischen präsentischen Flexionsstamm gebildet.“

translations.source_sense_description: Linguistik: die Zeitform Präteritum betreffend, unter Verwendung des Präteritums

glosses: Showing an action at a determined moment in the past.

examples.text: The Dravidian preterite tense is ordinarily formed, like the present, by annexing the pronominal signs to the preterite verbal participle.

glosses: Belonging wholly to the past; passed by.

examples.text: Without leaving your elbow-chair, you shall go back with me thirty years, which will bring you among things and persons as thoroughly preterite as Romulus or Numa.
Boas, Benedict, Malinowski, Radcliffe-Brown, Murdock, Evans-Pritchard, Griaule, Levi-Strauss, to keep the list short, preterite, and variegated, […]

glosses: A grammatical tense or verb form serving to denote events that took place or were completed in the past.

examples.text: When simple verbs redouble the preterite, the compounds drop the first syllable, as: Pello, pĕpŭli, to drive away, to beat back; Repello, rĕpŭli, and not rĕpĕpŭli, to drive back, to repel.
Nevertheless, a small amount of variation still exists in one area of standard English verbal morphology: the preterite and past participle forms of certain irregular verbs.
